coverage: 27 first-level divisions: 24 oblasts, Autonomous Republic of Crimea, Kyiv and Sevastopol. Sevastopol’s full administrative extent replaces the source’s urban footprint using a 2017 OSM/geoBoundaries polygon clipped to the same land silhouette; territorial sea is excluded. Also 126 mainland raions under the 2020 reform, from the September 2025 OCHA COD-AB v05 reference reviewed December 2025. Crimea is included as internationally recognised Ukrainian territory, with a visible UN-sourced occupation note. No live front line is implied. Crimea child boundaries are omitted because of source nesting exceptions; Kyiv and Sevastopol are not duplicated as raions. The Chornobyl exclusion-zone pseudo-unit is omitted. Regional population estimates are dated 1 January 2022, before the full-scale invasion, and exclude unavailable Crimea/Sevastopol values; no current regional figures are invented. National figures are separately sourced World Bank estimates. Inland lakes/reservoirs are removed using the retained Natural Earth reference, which may predate local shoreline changes. The drained Kakhovka Reservoir polygon is explicitly excluded from the old water mask; remaining river/floodplain detail is not presented as a current survey.
processing: Full available source resolution retained, cleaned together and rounded to six decimal places. Shared internal edges stored once; unselected coasts have no stroke. Deeper geometry loads only for the selected region. All views use the shared regional renderer, selected-outline index, adaptive detail, lifecycle and three-country cache. Territorial waters are excluded from land fills. Territory context features carry their own destination bounds.
